### MEDIUM: Dev and prod apps share one bundle ID, signing identity and keychain group, so side\-by\-side installs share hardware\-bound credentials
[\.github/workflows/release\-swift\.yml:15](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/1196b0fea4ae104a940f5dd700200fb62dded376/.github/workflows/release-swift.yml#L15) · A-002, A-015, T-055, T-058

The header comment states that dev releases install beside production while the bundle identifier and signing identity stay identical\. The Info\.plist step keeps CFBundleIdentifier=io\.darkbloom\.provider, and the same provisioning profile and keychain\-access\-group are embedded\. Dev apps are published on every master push without a tag\. On one Mac, a dev build can therefore load the production persistent SE key \(label io\.darkbloom\.provider\.attestation\-signing\.v2\) and the same\-app\-ID App Attest credential\. This lets a dev\-channel binary sign attestation or challenges for the production identity\. The same SE public key is also visible to both the dev and prod coordinators, which links the two environments' sessions\. Existing controls such as binary\-hash and CodeDirectory qualification and the per\-connection process X25519 key limit the damage\. Even so, this weakens the dev/prod credential separation that T\-055 and T\-058 assume\. Fix: give the dev app a distinct bundle ID, keychain label or access group \(and profile\), or document and test that dev builds cannot use production credentials\. Update the threat model either way\.
